world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog kone1241 lists no grammar/phonology; only Koneraw Swadesh wordlist found on archive.org

new_statements.quote: De hoofdklemtoon valt steeds op de laatste lettergreep, tenzij deze een toonlooze uitgang is, hetgeen wordt aangegeven, door op den klinker het teeken ˘ te plaatsen. Van de laatste lettergreep verspringt de bijklemtoon trocheevormig naar voren. In 't Digoeleesch valt de klemtoon vaak op de voorlaatste.
new_statements.translation: The main stress always falls on the last syllable, unless that is a stressless ending, which is indicated by placing the sign ˘ (breve) on the vowel. From the last syllable the secondary stress skips forward [leftward] in trochaic fashion. In Digul [Muyu-South] the stress often falls on the penultimate.
new_statements.citation: Geurtjens, H. 1933. Marindineesch-Nederlandsch Woordenboek. Verhandelingen van het Koninklijk Bataviaasch Genootschap van Kunsten en Wetenschappen 71(5). Bandoeng: Nix. Aanhangsel: Woordenlijsten der talen die het Marindineesche taalgebied begrenzen, pp. 397-429.
new_statements.locator: p. 397, 'N.B.' preceding the wordlists (last paragraph); Konerawsch column with breves on p. 398 (tsjirĕ 'tand', bandĕr 'slaap') and p. 410 (déw atsjoerĕ, dewasoedĕ)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (Geurtjens 1933 p. 397, Aanhangsel 'Woordenlijsten der talen die het Marindineesche taalgebied begrenzen', rendered from the open archive.org DLI scan../bian1251/). The last paragraph of the N.B. reads exactly as quoted: 'De hoofdklemtoon valt steeds op de laatste lettergreep, tenzij deze een toonlooze uitgang is, hetgeen wordt aangegeven, door op den klinker het teeken ˘ te plaatsen. Van de laatste lettergreep verspringt de bijklemtoon trocheevormig naar voren. In 't Digoeleesch valt de klemtoon vaak op de voorlaatste.' The preceding paragraphs confirm acute = vowel length and grave = 'gebroken' (open) vowel quality, so neither marks stress. The scanned copy (../bian1251/ ~line 7694…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress on the final syllable of the word; when the final syllable is a 'toneless ending' (marked with a breve in the transcription) it is skipped and stress is on the preceding syllable. Geurtjens applies this to all seven bordering-language lists he transcribed, Konerawsch included; the breve is in fact used on Koneraw forms, so the transcriber did apply the rule to Koneraw. Note that in his notation acute = vowel length and grave = open vowel quality, neither marks stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated: secondary stress ('bijklemtoon') alternates trochaically leftward from the final main-stressed syllable, i.e. on every second syllable counting back from the end.
new_statements.exceptions: Final syllables that are stressless endings (breve) do not take stress; the only language singled out as different is Digoeleesch (often penultimate), so Koneraw falls under the general final rule. Consistent with the sister language Mombum, whose own sketch (Drabbe 1950: 562) says stress is mostly final, but on the first syllable in trisyllables with secondary on the last.
new_statements.domain_note: Blanket transcription convention for the citation forms of eight short wordlists (c. 450 items, Koneraw among them) collected by a missionary lexicographer in 1933; not a Koneraw-specific phonological study and no phonological analysis exists for Koneraw at all. Word-level, citation forms; nothing on phrase stress. Wordlist reflects an older stage of the language (Usher & Suter 2020: 154).
new_statements.identity_note: The only statement is Geurtjens's (1933: 397) blanket transcription note covering all seven 'bordering-language' wordlists (Kaladdarsch and Teri-Kalwasch = Kimaghama, Konerawsch = Koneraw kone1241, Komelomsch = Mombum nucl1452, Jabsch = Southern Yelmek, Jeisch = Yei, Digoeleesch = Muyu-South), with Digoeleesch explicitly excepted; it is applied to Koneraw (breves on Koneraw forms, pp. 398, 410) but is not a Koneraw-specific phonological description. Footnote 1 on p. 398 identifies Konerawsch as the language spoken at the place of the same name on Frederik Hendrik Island, i.e. Glottolog kone1241 [kdw]. No grammar, sketch or phonology of Koneraw exists (Glottolog 5.1: 0 descriptive refs); catalog entry, if made, should be flagged as a transcriber's convention of low evidential weight.

Van de laatste lettergreep verspringt de bijklemtoon trocheevormig naar voren. In 't Digoeleesch valt de klemtoon vaak op de voorlaatste.
sources.locator: p. 397, 'N.B.' preceding the wordlists (last paragraph); Konerawsch column with breves on p. 398 (tsjirĕ 'tand', bandĕr 'slaap') and p. 410 (déw atsjoerĕ, dewasoedĕ)
sources.note: Transcriber's blanket note for all seven bordering-language wordlists (Konerawsch included), p. 397: main stress always on the last syllable unless that is a 'toonlooze uitgang' (marked with a breve); secondary stress alternates trochaically leftward from the last syllable; only Digoeleesch often has penultimate stress. Acute = vowel length, grave = open vowel quality, not stress. The breve does appear in the Konerawsch column (p. 398 tsjire-breve 'tooth', bande-breve-r 'sleep'; p. 410 dew atsjoere-breve, dewasoede-breve), so the rule was applied to Koneraw words.

sources.note: No stress information; ~200 glossed forms without source note; the acute marks on some forms (gha, yederi, tunnebe, me, dew, yow) are Geurtjens's vowel-length marks carried over, not stress.

sources.note: Silent. 'The only data in this language which have been published, is a wordlist of about 450 items (Geurtjens 1933, pp. 398-433)... The list does not contain any information on the grammatical structure of Koneraw; only the pronouns can be given here.' (Pronouns no/yu/ungumi, ni/imu/tonte.)
